post.caption: Tiffany's windows hid two famous artists. In the 1950s, Robert Rauschenberg and Jasper Johns dressed store windows in New York to pay their bills. Two of their clients were Bonwit Teller and Tiffany. Gene Moore, who ran Tiffany's windows, hired them. They worked under a fake firm name, Matson Jones Custom Display. Rauschenberg wrote that their shame forced them to take that name. Their Tiffany windows ran from 1956 to 1958. One put jewelry in plaster cast caves. In another, a diamond ring spilled from a painted pomegranate. A spider web showed cocktail earrings. Their last documented Tiffany window, in 1958, was paper birds.
